answer: A collateral bonding protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock crypto assets in escrow before trading. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of committing scarce liquid capital per identity. Escrow releases move at the pace of a glacier, preventing adversarial bots that wander across ephemeral keys from evading fraud proofs before their slashed stake becomes a burned relic. A key limitation is that mandatory deposits exclude capital-constrained honest agents.
